speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: It is important we narrow these differences to ensure social cohesion is not impacted.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: First, we need to enable our ITE and polytechnic graduates to enter good quality, in-demand jobs so that they can enjoy good career prospects and sustained wage growth.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Our ITE and polytechnics regularly review their curricula to ensure their industry relevance and this includes aligning with the skills framework and the Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs).

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: They also work closely with employers and sector agencies to provide quality internships to students, equipping them with skills to enter good jobs related to their training.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Additionally, MOE is scaling up Work-Study Programmes, where fresh polytechnic and ITE graduates are placed into jobs where they can deepen their skills through a structured training programme that includes on-the-job training, while pursuing careers related to their disciplines of study.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: MOE regularly tracks the effectiveness and relevance of these Work-Study Programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: And based on MOE's latest survey findings, median salaries had also increased compared to what they received at the start of the programme.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This is complemented by new sector-specific programmes, which were launched last year.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: To Dr Wan Rizal’s question on how we plan to engage with employers, IMDA, together with industry players, has set up the TechSkills Accelerator, or TeSA programme for short, for ITE and Polytechnics Alliance, or the TIP Alliance in short, to equip our polytechnic and ITE graduates with the skills to kickstart their careers in tech.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The TIP Alliance will work with participating companies such as Accenture, Google and Singtel to provide internships and apprenticeships.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: MTI has also introduced the Accelerated Pathways for Technicians and Assistant Engineers for Manufacturing, or APT(M) to support manufacturing companies with progressive HR practices in hiring and training ITE graduates for Technician and Assistant Engineer roles, and providing them with career, skills progression and competitive salaries.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As our economy continues to restructure, as it continues to transform, jobs as well as careers will also keep evolving.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The National Centre of Excellence for Workplace Learning, or NACE helps companies to strengthen their workplace learning capabilities, so that their workers can upskill on the job.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: ITE and Polytechnic graduates can pursue modular upgrading or part-time full qualification programmes at the Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) while they are working.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: These modular courses can stack up to diploma, post-diploma and degree qualifications.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Over time, workers may also consider pivoting to new careers as interests change and new opportunities emerge in the economy.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Workforce Singapore (WSG) offers close to 100 Career Conversion Programmes, or CCPs, across about 30 sectors, to help workers to transition into new in-demand jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Thirdly, we also need employers to consider ITE and Polytechnic graduates fairly for job and promotion opportunities and prospects, instead of being pigeonholed unfairly based on their starting qualifications.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices set out fair and merit-based employment practices that all employers should adopt when making employment decisions.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices, or TAFEP, has been supporting employers with advisory services and resources to implement fair practices.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: In addition, the Institute for HR Professionals (IHRP) works closely with enterprises and HR professionals to strengthen overall HR capabilities, such as via the Human Capital Diagnostic Tool (HCDT) to identify developmental areas and upskill HR in fair and progressive practices via IHRP skill badges.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: I have outlined our very comprehensive approach to ensure that our ITE and polytechnic graduates will continue to enjoy good career prospects and for them to achieve their fullest potential.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Success will require buy-in from everyone in society to do our part to recognise, to value one another, and to embrace a broader definition of meritocracy.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: My concern is really about the growing divergence in the starting pay of the ITE, the polytechnic and the university students.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: My greatest concern really is over time, this gap widens, it increases and it is very difficult to catch up over time.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Having taught students from ITE and right now in polytechnics too, I can see the potential in them especially when they come back to do their part-time diplomas or degrees.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: But they do feel that because they had started way further, it becomes more difficult for them to come forward.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Many of this issue stems from the issue of stigmatisation.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: And that is why I ask in the Parliamentary Question what are the measures that the Ministry would take to change the mindset among employers?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: But at the same time, can we set a timeline for an implementation?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: At the very least, we can give ourselves this idea that we are going toward somewhere.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: And we can give our ITE and polytechnic graduates that idea that we are trying our best to close this gap.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: In that regard, would we be willing to start a longitudinal and continual study, and data collection on the pay gap between the different groups so that we can use this data to supplement our policy planning?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Members of the House, this is an ongoing exercise.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: This includes the graduate employment survey as well as the comprehensive labour force survey.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We believe that by investing in this and by continually helping them to upgrade, to re-skill, to keep relevant to the rapidly changing disruptions that we are seeing around us, they will then be able to, as a result of the re-skilling and the upgrading, improve their wages as well as their career prospects.
